\subsection{Normative language}

``Shall'' is a contract requirement. ``May'' identifies an allowed form whose
scientific preconditions still have to be met. ``Exact'' means exact with
respect to the declared mathematical realization and its declared numerical
identity; it does not mean that nature, calibration, or the parent data are
known without uncertainty. ``Unknown'' and ``unavailable'' never mean zero.
An option in Section~\ref{sec:authored-options} is a decision candidate, not a
selected route.

\subsection{Objects, domains, and indexing}

An application location is denoted by $x$ and a parent-map sample by $z$.
Both are coordinates in one declared map-domain chart with an immutable WCS,
frame, grouping, pixel measure, and indexing order. The admitted parent field
is real-valued, $m:\Dom_m\rightarrow\R$, and the unit-amplitude template
centered or anchored at $x$ is real-valued,
$t_x:\Supp_t(x)\rightarrow\R$. The physical template amplitude $A$, the
published amplitude $\widehat A$, and the contractions $N$ and $D$ are real
scalars. Let $\mathcal X_{\rm in}$ be the real vector space of admitted parent
samples, $\mathcal X_{\rm out}$ the real vector space of published amplitude
samples, and $\mathcal X_{\rm anc}$ the real vector space indexing template
anchors. Then $L:\mathcal X_{\rm in}\rightarrow\mathcal X_{\rm out}$ and
$R_t:\mathcal X_{\rm anc}\rightarrow\mathcal X_{\rm out}$. The restriction
of any field $u$ to the samples required at $x$ is $u_x$. The realized linear
weighting operator is a real linear map $Q_x$ on the admitted parent-sample
space, and its declared null space is $\Null(Q_x)$.

The bracket
\[
  \langle a,b\rangle_x
  = \sum_{z\in\Supp_t(x)} a(z)^{*} b(z)\,\mu(z)
\]
denotes the declared discrete inner product. A continuum representation may
replace the sum by an integral only when the measure, sampling relation, and
equivalence to the published discrete estimand are declared. Here $\mu(z)$ is
the declared pixel or quadrature measure. Complex conjugation is explicit so
the same notation can be used for a complex transform representation. Such a
representation may use coefficients in $\C$, but it shall preserve the
conjugate symmetry of real fields, use the Hermitian adjoint for transform-
domain operators, and induce the same real $Q_x$, $N$, $D$, $L$, and
$\widehat A$ after inverse transformation. Complex transform coefficients do
not change the real scientific codomains above. In the real sample basis,
covariances are real symmetric matrices and ordinary transpose is therefore
the covariance adjoint. The contract does not assume stationarity, isotropy,
periodicity, a flat sky, or a Euclidean pixel metric unless the selected
realization declares and validates it.

\begin{longtable}{p{0.19\linewidth}p{0.71\linewidth}}
\toprule
Symbol & Normative meaning \\
\midrule
\endhead
$m$, $m_x$ & Immutable admitted ordinary-MAP observation or coadd parent, and
its complete restriction needed at $x$. \\
$t_x$ & Immutable materialized parent-map response for unit template amplitude
at $x$; its scaling fixes the amplitude convention. \\
$Q_x$ & Frozen realized weighting operator. It is inverse covariance only
when exact covariance authority establishes that identity. \\
$N(x)$ & Weighted template-parent contraction
$\langle t_x,Q_xm_x\rangle_x$. \\
$D(x)$ & Weighted template self-contraction
$\langle t_x,Q_xt_x\rangle_x$; normalization unless exact inverse-covariance
GLS premises establish a variance interpretation. \\
$\widehat A(x)$ & Published template-amplitude estimand $N(x)/D(x)$ at an
admitted location. \\
$L_x$ & Fixed-state linear functional that maps a compatible parent field to
$\widehat A(x)$. \\
$R_t(x,y)$ & Fixed-state response $L_x t_y$ to a unit template anchored at
$y$. \\
$C_{\rm parent}$ & Authorized real symmetric parent covariance on
$\mathcal X_{\rm in}$ for an explicitly named population and conditioning
state. \\
$C_{\rm cond}$ & Conditional covariance of the filtered amplitude field,
$L C_{\rm parent}L^{\mathsf T}$ on $\mathcal X_{\rm out}$, when every premise
is authorized. \\
$g$ & Immutable method/state generation. A successor is a distinct identity. \\
$\Valid$ & Set of locations satisfying every parent, template, support,
operator, normalization, unit, calibration, and selected-option predicate. \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

\subsection{Quantity and unit convention}

The template is the expected parent-map response per unit amplitude. Therefore
\[
  [\widehat A] = [m]/[t].
\]
A point-source flux interpretation exists only if the template producer and
CAL/BEAM lineage establish that exact amplitude convention. Otherwise
$\widehat A$ is a shape amplitude. Parent beam, DC or integral response,
extended-source fidelity, matched-filter solid angle, and calibration
covariance are not inherited by implication.
